slides.headline: Apple said no to AI training. Now yes.
What changed this week
slides.body: Apple published a research paper detailing how it will use your device data to improve its AI models.

slides.headline: What data they want
slides.body: Your emails, messages, photos, and app usage — processed on your iPhone, then summarized and sent to Apple.

slides.headline: Why the reversal matters
slides.body: Apple built its brand on privacy. This move lets them compete with Google and OpenAI, but breaks their core promise.

slides.headline: The catch you should know
slides.body: Apple says data stays anonymous. But researchers have re-identified 'anonymous' datasets before. Opt-out details are still vague.

slides.headline: Want the plain-English version?
slides.body: Follow for AI news that actually affects your phone, not code.
